scope: Integrate the five themes throughout the existing nine-part narrative, preserving the original narrative blocks and established chart layout.

integration.1: Distributed solar generation beyond utility statistics; consumer resilience and grid flexibility.
integration.2: LNG supplier concentration, Hormuz disruption, fuel prices and foreign-exchange exposure.
integration.3: Fixed obligations spread across fewer grid units, with an explicitly illustrative calculation.
integration.4: Unequal access to self-generation; distinguish reduced purchases, losses and unpaid bills.
integration.5: Rigid LNG contracts, possible surpluses and supply shocks; separate gas and power arrears.
integration.6: Thar coal trade-offs, ETIP, financing horizons, and conditional NDC targets.
integration.7: Battery storage, electrified transport, charging needs and the new-sales NEV target.
integration.8: Industrial solar/storage/grid combinations, auction storage requirements and SME access.
integration.9: Avoided fuel imports and solar resilience, with a conditional forecast separated from estimated cumulative savings.

clarifications: Generation shares use the dated Ember/Renewables First FY23–FY25 estimate (10% to 28%), distinct from installed capacity and calendar-year datasets.
Battery 7.6 GWh is cumulative over 2018–2025; annual 2024/2025 chart values are 1.43/4.59 GWh. Energy and power units are not interchanged.
Avoided imports >$12 billion are cumulative through February 2026. $6.3 billion is an additional conditional projection, not an audited full-year result.
NEV 30% is a target for new sales in 2030. The 3,000 charging-station figure is a policy objective, not an operating-station count.
NEPRA’s 10% requirement is a firm-capacity ratio for a specified wheeling auction, not a nationwide rooftop mandate.
Climate investment estimates cover different horizons and broader sectors. The 33% conditional component means percentage points of projected 2035 emissions, not 33% of funding.
Fixed-cost pressure is a transparent illustration, not observed solar-related tariff growth.
